newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end higher, gains precarious.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end higher, gains precarious.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended modestly higher in technically driven trade on Thursday but dealers said the gains could be precarious as bearish factors continued to cloud Japan's corporate sector and economy.
The lead Nikkei 225 September contract ended up 70 points to 19,765 after trading between 19,600 and 19,840 on low volume.
"I think 19,800-19,900 would be a good level to go short now. I expect the market to go back down," a trader at a Japanese brokerage said.
He said news of a medium-sized construction firm asking for court protection last week sparked fears of more such cases.
He said the September Nikkei could test 19,600 with a breach of that level pushing it down towards 19,400.
"I think it should pause around 19,400 for a while and it may test 19,000 later on," he added.
But a trader at a local institution said a close above the 19,750 level boded well for further upside although 20,000 would continue to present a stiff barrier.
In Taiwan futures, the July contract ended higher at 401.6 on volume of 1,583 lots.
The contract drew strong institutional interest throughout the session due to its large discount to the cash index, Refco Singapore Pte Ltd said in a daily market commentary.
